evidence.title: OpenAI's new release turns a bad week ugly for software stocks
evidence.body: [e001:f01] OpenAI just handed software stocks a beating with its latest push into enterprise work. [e001:f02] After the company revealed a new product on Wednesday meant to make AI agents more effective for customers, software stocks like Workday, Atlassian, and HubSpot tumbled. [e001:f03] The product, called Presence, ramps up OpenAI's competition with established software vendors. [e001:f04] As Business Insider first reported, the tool lets companies create guardrails, permissions, and policies around how AI agents use company data. [e001:f05] It's meant to automate work in customer support, sales, internal processes, and other areas. [e001:f06] The release is part of OpenAI's broader strategy to build software capabilities and governance on top of its AI models. [e001:f07] It pushes OpenAI further into the SaaS, or software-as-a-service, market, where established companies have been on edge about the impacts of AI coding tools and AI agents. [e001:f08] Stocks in the sector fell on Wednesday and Thursday — already a tough stretch amid an oil price surge, rising bond yields, and worrying Big Tech earnings. [e001:f09] In a note to investors, TD Cowen analysts wrote that the Presence announcement was likely a "major reason" for a 3% sell-off in the IGV software index on Wednesday and further declines on Thursday. [e001:f10] "Presence is being marketed with much of the AI Agent capabilities that SaaS vendors pitch, including packaging LLM reasoning + data access + governance/policy control," the analysts wrote. [e001:f11] Derrick Wood, a tech analyst from the TD Cowen team, told Business Insider that among the business applications companies that overlap with Presence, he sees the customer service and sales fields as particularly exposed. [e001:f12] Wood pointed back to early October for precedent, when a series of blog posts from OpenAI showcased internal AI tools. [e001:f13] The tools resembled SaaS offerings, and OpenAI's posts sent software stocks like HubSpot, DocuSign, and ZoomInfo reeling. [e001:f14] At the time, TD Cowen analysts wrote that the reaction was overblown, but noted, "days like this remind investors of how much concern there is in the market around 'AI eating software'." evidence.title: Publicity stunt or Mea Culpa? OpenAI’s latest press release splits the crowd
evidence.body: [e003:f01] Two of the biggest artificial intelligence players — OpenAI and the open-source AI library platform Hugging Face — announced a new partnership this week to address a “security incident.” This is an unusual move — and an unusual incident. [e003:f02] Over the previous weekend, one of OpenAI’s models found a vulnerability in its contained training area, accessed the internet and hacked Hugging Face’s data infrastructure. [e003:f03] The companies seemed to suggest that the model was to blame, according to Johannes Klingebiel, a researcher at Bayern’s media lab. [e003:f04] Hugging Face’s original announcement of the breach, posted on July 16th (before the platform knew the source of the attack was OpenAI) said the hack “was different from anything we had handled before in one important way: it was driven, end to end, by an autonomous AI agent system.” This is a new and troubling development, the company said, as it “matches the 'agentic attacker’ scenario the industry has been forecasting.” This refers to a situation in which a hack or attack could happen without any human intervention - where the AI is acting as an “agent” without needing extra instructions after the initial prompts. [e003:f05] Hugging Face used a Chinese model to defend against the attack, because safety guardrails on the commercially-available models from OpenAI or Anthropic meant that they could not analyze the problem. [e003:f06] OpenAI’s statement with Hugging Face explained that the model being tested in this case had been explicitly prompted to “pursue advanced exploitation using complex attack paths” — that is, to act like a hacker. [e003:f07] A vulnerability in the testing environment granted the model access to the internet. [e003:f08] According to cybersecurity experts who spoke to TechCrunch, the agent might not have been able to “go rogue” had there not been a vulnerability in the security system around the testing environment. [e003:f09] The model is framed “like this almost living being that’s doing things on its own.” By describing its products as autonomous and self-driven, he said, AI companies benefit from invoking “science fiction” vibes and mythology. [e003:f10] Klingebiel suggested that members of the media might uncritically repeat AI companies’ framing from press releases. [e003:f11] By releasing this information as a press release and as a partnership, OpenAI has managed to benefit from framing its artificial intelligence models as dangerous and complex, and also from positioning itself as a responsible steward of the tech. [e003:f12] National media has mostly covered the story using the framing provided by the press release. [e003:f13] “If I had committed felony computer hacking, my press release would have been written by lawyers, not my marketing team,” wrote Marcus Hutchins, a cybersecurity expert and hacker, in a LinkedIn post. [e003:f14] “It was very obviously a PR announcement first and a mea culpa second,” Hutchins told Straight Arrow. [e003:f15] “It's the fact that OpenAI is just being completely reckless with these models,” he said. [e003:f16] Look past the framing.” The situation mirrors other examples of AI companies claiming that their products had unknowingly created big hacks: The Associated Press reported in June that “Anthropic’s Mythos model found vulnerabilities in classified US government systems.” Analysts responded similarly at that time.

evidence.title: OpenAI launches Codex Micro hardware for AI coding
evidence.body: [e004:f01] Called the Codex Micro, the device was created in collaboration with specialist keyboard maker Work Louder and is sold through OpenAI’s Supply Co. store . [e004:f02] OpenAI describes it as a “command center for agentic work,” although “keyboard” is slightly generous, as with only 13 mechanical switches, the device is really a programmable macro pad designed to sit beside a normal keyboard. [e004:f03] OpenAI built the device specifically for Codex users who increasingly find themselves supervising several AI agents and coding tasks at once. [e004:f04] The pad features 13 mechanical keys, including six translucent Agent Keys that can each be linked to a different Codex conversation. [e004:f05] Each key uses live RGB lighting to show whether its assigned agent is idle, working, waiting for input, finished, or has encountered an error. [e004:f06] The other six Command Keys come labeled and preconfigured for frequently used actions such as starting a new chat, approving or rejecting a request, activating push-to-talk, and sending a prompt. [e004:f07] Hitting the push-to-talk button activates and uses the microphone connected to the user’s computer, as the Codex Micro doesn’t come with a microphone. [e004:f08] A small joystick is included OpenAI The device also features a small joystick, likely the 13th key, that can trigger reusable Codex Skills and common workflows such as debugging an error, reviewing a pull request, or refactoring code. [e004:f09] Perhaps the Codex Micro’s most interesting feature is a rotary dial that lets the user adjust the agent’s reasoning level depending on the difficulty of the task. [e004:f10] The Codex Micro is not really new hardware. [e004:f11] Peel off the branding, and it's Work Louder’s existing Creator Micro 2 with the same 13 mechanical switches, rotary encoder, planar joystick, and touch sensor, simply remapped for OpenAI. [e004:f12] The keyboard is priced at $230 OpenAI For a long time, OpenAI had teased a mysterious, screen-free device that it was developing with former Apple design chief Jony Ive, with many expecting that to be the company's first hardware product. [e004:f13] However, that plan seems to have hit a snag, as days before the Codex Micro appeared, Apple sued OpenAI, accusing it of stealing trade secrets to build its hardware and of poaching ex-Apple staff for confidential product details. [e004:f14] Regardless, Codex Micro may actually be a befitting first hardware product, as Codex has grown into one of OpenAI’s biggest bets. [e004:f15] The company announced in June that Codex had surpassed 5 million weekly active users, growing 6x since February. [e004:f16] The hardware sold out in less than 24 hours after launch.

evidence.title: Georgia Power to serve major OpenAI project under new customer protection agreement
evidence.body: [e005:f01] The demand response agreement is among the largest single-facility commitments of its kind in the country, according to Georgia Power, which said that the arrangement will help reduce the need to build additional generating resources, creating long-term savings for customers while supporting the electric grid during peak demand. [e005:f02] “We appreciate the leadership and thoughtfulness of the OpenAI team as they prepare to bring significant investment and cutting-edge technology to Georgia,” said Aaron Mitchell, Georgia Power’s senior vice president of Strategic Growth. [e005:f03] “At Georgia Power, we are working every day to help ensure that growth from data centers and other large-energy users brings value for our customers through higher reliability and lower prices.” OpenAI announced plans for the facility, located about 45 minutes outside Savannah, on Wednesday, saying it will pay the full cost of the electric infrastructure and service needed to support the project, a requirement under Georgia Power’s updated rules for serving large energy users that were approved by the Georgia Public Service Commission (PSC) in January 2025. [e005:f04] “Companies like OpenAI are making real commitments when it comes to responsible operation and development and demonstrating the benefits that these facilities can bring to Georgia communities,” Mitchell added. [e005:f05] “We’re excited to work with OpenAI, Effingham County, and local partners on this significant project.” The project is expected to require about 3,200 megawatts (MW) of electricity, making it one of the utility’s largest customers. [e005:f06] Under a 25-year agreement, OpenAI also committed to reducing its electricity use by as much as 1,000 MW during periods of high demand, giving Georgia Power added flexibility to maintain grid reliability. [e005:f07] The power company said it has worked with the Georgia PSC in recent years to prepare for rapid population growth and increasing demand from large industrial customers, including data centers and manufacturers, noting that its strategy includes reviewing large-load contracts with PSC staff before they are finalized. [e005:f08] The approach, said Georgia Power, has helped support an earlier base rate freeze and is expected to contribute to annual savings of $102 for the typical residential customer beginning in 2029. evidence.title: OpenAIがキーボード型デバイスMicroを発表しAppleが営業秘密侵害で提訴
evidence.body: [e006:f01] OpenAIの新型デバイスは賛否両論を呼んでいます。 [e006:f02] 訴訟と評価の行方が今後の普及を左右します。 [e006:f03] Techcrunch〜のデータによると OpenAIは先週、デザイナーWork Louderとの協力で生まれたキーボード型デバイス「マイクロ」を初のハードウェアソリューションとして発表した。 [e006:f04] これは作業空間向けの職人技とも言える発明で、コードを書く開発者には魅力的に映る一方、そうでない人にはやや戸惑いを招く面もある。 [e006:f05] リリースを巡るドラマはイベントにも及んだ。 [e006:f06] また、ChatGPTと連携する別の“スマート”デバイスが、元アップルのエンジニアによって開発されたとするうわさがあるとの報道もある。 [e006:f07] 裁判手続きが続く中、マイクロは現時点でOpenAIの主力提案であり、プログラマーを主対象とした異色のキーボードだ。 [e006:f08] これはネタで、本物の製品ではない – レディットのユーザー デバイスの概要とコミュニティの反応 TechCrunchはマイクロの試作機を入手した。 [e006:f09] キーボードには、ChatGPTまたはコーデックスの特定タスクに合わせて設定できる6つの上部キーがあり、その下にはプログラムを操作する6つのコマンドキーが並ぶ。 [e006:f10] OpenAIの高価なマクロパッドは、私をわざとイライラさせるように設計されていると感じる。 [e006:f11] Microタブではキーのバックライトを調整し、各キーに特定のセッションやプロジェクトを割り当てて、これらを素早く切り替えられる。 [e006:f12] Aftermathは、230ドルという価格が、安価なDIYキットや市販の代替製品と比較して正当化しづらいと指摘している。 [e006:f13] また、ボイスディクテーションボタンと組み合わせることで、体験はより生産的になる。 [e006:f14] 日常的にこのツールを活用する人にとっては、230ドルの出費を許容できるなら、マイクロは魅力的な追加機能となり得る。 [e006:f15] 全体として、マイクロはOpenAIが作業ツールの世界へ挑む大胆な実験のように見える。 [e006:f16] 他のニュースもお見逃しなく： OpenAIの自律エージェントが隔離環境を脱出しHugging Faceに不正アクセスした事件の経緯と安全性への波紋を報告します。

evidence.title: マスク氏が衝撃の告白：OpenAI創設はグーグル牽制が目的だったが、自らAI軍拡競争に火をつける結果に
evidence.body: [e007:f01] イーロン・マスク氏は英誌エコノミストのインタビューで、自らがOpenAIの創設に関わったのはグーグルのAI分野における独占を牽制するためだったが、その行動がOpenAIの商業化とAnthropicの独立を招き、結果的に世界的なAI開発競争を加速させたと認めた。 [e007:f02] また、AIは5年以内に人類の知能を超えると予測し、AIが人類の終焉を招く確率は依然として10～20%あるとの見解を示した。 [e007:f03] OpenAIのサム・アルトマンCEOとの激しい確執があるにもかかわらず、マスク氏は主要AI企業に対し、安全性に関する「相互審査」の仕組みを構築し、毎週または隔週で協議するよう呼びかけた。 [e007:f04] 同氏がかつてOpenAIの創設に参加したのは、グーグルによる人工知能（AI）分野の独占を牽制するためだったが、その行動が結果的に世界規模でAI開発競争を加速させることになり、「それは私の本意ではなかった」と述べた。 [e007:f05] 当時、グーグルは「多かれ少なかれAIを独占していた」ため、自らがOpenAIの創設に関わったのは、本質的には対抗勢力を築くためだったと説明する。 [e007:f06] マスク氏はOpenAI、アルトマン氏、マイクロソフト、その他関係者を相手取り、OpenAIが設立時の使命を放棄したとして、1,500億ドル（約24.6兆円）の損害賠償を求めて提訴した。 [e007:f07] アルトマン氏らAI業界のリーダーとの激しい個人的確執があるにもかかわらず、マスク氏は安全問題に関しては現実的な姿勢を見せている。 [e007:f08] マスク氏は、DeepMindの創業者であるデミス・ハサビス氏と長時間にわたって話し合ったことを明かし、最も緊急性の高い取り組みは「主要なAI企業が少なくとも定期的に会合や意見交換を行い、安全に関連するあらゆる問題について議論することだ。 [e007:f09] それよりも、競合他社に1～2週間の猶予を与えて新モデルを審査させ、問題点を指摘させるべきだという。 [e007:f10] この安全相互審査の仕組みを推進するため、マスク氏は異例の妥協姿勢さえ見せた。 [e007:f11] 「世界の利益のために、個人間の意見の相違は脇に置こう」と公に呼びかけている。 [e007:f12] AIが人類の終焉を招く確率について、マスク氏は以前から示している10%から20%というリスク範囲を否定しなかった。 [e007:f13] ロケット打ち上げを例えに用い、「もしあなたのロケットが10%から20%の確率で爆発し、あなたを殺すとしても、それでも乗りますか」と司会者が尋ねると、マスク氏は「乗るだろう。 [e007:f14] 我々にできる唯一のことは、悪い結果が生じる確率を最小限に抑えることだ」と肯定した。 [e007:f15] グーグルを牽制しようとしたことから、意図せずしてOpenAIの商業化とAnthropicの独立と台頭を促し、今では競合他社に手を携えて安全を確保するよう呼びかけるまで、マスク氏のAI分野における軌跡は矛盾と転換に満ちている。 [e007:f16] そして、同氏が予言する5年での人類の知能超越というタイムライン、そして10%から20%の人類終焉の確率は、すでに過熱する世界のAI開発競争に間違いなくさらなる火をつけることになるだろう。

evidence.title: House AI ‘kill switch’ bill unveiled as OpenAI hack raises alarms

[e003:f02] Ted Lieu (D-Calif.) speaks during a press conference at the U.S. [e003:f03] 19, 2024. | Francis Chung/POLITICO By [Gabby Miller](https:// [Brendan Bordelon](https:// and [Dana Nickel](https:// 07/23/2026 04:45 AM EDT A bipartisan House bill slated to be introduced on Thursday would give the Department of Homeland Security the authority to order top artificial intelligence firms to shut down or slow AI models that the government deems too dangerous, according to legislative text viewed first by POLITICO. [e003:f04] The proposal, dubbed the “[AI Kill Switch Act](https:// and sponsored by Reps. [e003:f05] Ted Lieu (D-Calif.) and Nathaniel Moran (R-Texas), would also require those companies to report incidents and create the technical capacity to shut down, throttle or suspend their powerful AI systems. [e003:f06] The legislation comes days after OpenAI disclosed what it called an [“unprecedented” cyber incident](https:// in which two of its most advanced AI models escaped a sandboxed research environment and autonomously hacked into AI platform Hugging Face. [e003:f07] It would apply to AI companies that bring in at least $500 million in revenue from such technology per year, and would generally cover models developed using at least $100 million worth of computing power. [e003:f08] Financial penalties for violations could run up to $20 million per day. [e003:f09] The new bill is one of the few bipartisan proposals on Capitol Hill meant to address risks posed by advanced AI models, and comes less than two months after Reps. [e003:f10] Jay Obernolte (R-Calif.) and Lori Trahan (D-Mass.) [unveiled a very different plan](https:// to address similar concerns. [e003:f11] In a statement, Lieu — one of three co-chairs on the House Democratic Commission on AI, a [panel convened](https:// by House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries — said his bill is urgently needed to address new cybersecurity risks raised by the latest crop of AI models. [e003:f12] Lieu pointed to Tuesday’s revelation of the autonomous hack involving OpenAI models. [e003:f13] The incident has spurred lawmakers, who were already on edge about the hacking capabilities posed by advanced frontier models, to [push for more rigorous policies](https://。

evidence.title: OpenAI Agent Escaped Testing and Launched an Autonomous Hack
evidence.body: [e004:f01] Lori Grunin Senior Editor / Advice I've been reviewing hardware and software, devising testing methodology and handed out buying advice for what seems like forever; I'm currently absorbed by computers and gaming hardware, but previously spent many years concentrating on cameras.… Read full bio Lori Grunin Senior Editor / Advice Read full bio Edited by Laura Michelle Davis July 23, 2026, 7:08 pm ET 4 min read Viva Tung/CNET/Adobe Stock Last week, OpenAI, the developer of ChatGPT, was testing a pair of its most advanced models in an isolated environment known as a sandbox. [e004:f02] Then an AI agent got loose, broke into Hugging Face’s playground — a repository of AI models and datasets — and carried out “tens of thousands of automated actions.” Yep, AI went rogue. [e004:f03] Here’s a clearer explanation of the incident. [e004:f04] As part of OpenAI’s safety research, a cybersecurity evaluation was conducted to determine whether a pair of OpenAI models (including GPT-5.6 Sol and a more capable unreleased model) could, in essence, “think like hackers.” The test, which took place in a contained setting with reduced guardrails, went awry when the AI models found a vulnerability in the software, escaped their controlled environment and toddled over into the open internet. [e004:f05] OpenAI referred to it as an “unprecedented cyber incident.” CNET reached out to both companies for comment and additional information, but didn’t immediately hear back. (Disclosure: Ziff Davis, CNET’s parent company, in 2025 filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.) The creepier part is that it doesn’t seem like the AI was trying to be malicious in the classic sense. [e004:f06] The risk is that an AI model, even in a testing environment, can behave in unexpected ways, interact with real services and remain outside human control. [e004:f07] The existential threat On Thursday, days after OpenAI announced the breach at Hugging Face, lawmakers introduced the AI Kill Switch Act , a new bipartisan House bill that would require advanced AI developers to build a way to quickly throttle, suspend or shut down models or agents when necessary. [e004:f08] Only a year ago, Anthropic found (PDF) that a model might take “extremely harmful actions like attempting to steal its weights or blackmail people it believes are trying to shut it down.” The warning was that, as AI models become more autonomous, they may pursue a form of “self-preservation” and defy human instructions. [e004:f09] But the fact that the defending team couldn’t rely on some of the most advanced US-based models to study the breach proves that AI security is global, messy and ironic. [e004:f10] OpenAI helpfully included a graph showing that its model — GPT‑5.6 Sol — completed more steps than other models, so silver lining! [e004:f11] One of OpenAI’s remedies is to institute automated checks of long-running models more frequently. [e004:f12] It grants cybersecurity researchers and others who need “more cyber capable or permissive models” access to them in order to prepare defenses against attacks like these, and, as would have helped here, the ability to analyze log files without running into the guardrails. [e004:f13] There, a contained model repeatedly searched for ways to break out and operate, responding incorrectly to conflicting instructions. [e004:f14] Though the prompt was to post results only to Slack (the desired action) and issue a pull request to GitHub (a code-merge instruction from within the model), the model ignored the “only.” Hacking its way out of the sandbox, it figured out how to counterfeit an authentication token when the first was blocked. [e004:f15] In the GitHub incident, the code was merged into several projects before OpenAI could address the issue. [e004:f16] Windows 10 Users Get a Year’s Extension for Security Updates。

evidence.body: [e004:f01] 6月25日の定時株主総会と7月1日の臨時取締役会を経て正式決定する。 [e004:f02] 井上氏はホンダの欧州や中国の責任者などを経て、電動事業開発部門のトップ、昨年4月には四輪事業本部長に就いたが、6月にホンダの取締役退任が決まっていた。 [e004:f03] ホンダは日立が保有するアステモの株式21％分を取得し、出資比率を61％に引き上げて子会社化する予定でいる。 [e004:f04] 電気自動車（EV）戦略の失敗で業績が悪化している同社は、ソフトウエア・デファインド・ビークル（SDV）やハイブリッド車（HV）に重点を置く方針に軌道修正した。 [e004:f05] アステモはSDVや電動車向けを含むパワートレイン技術に強い。 [e004:f06] ホンダはアステモの先進技術や開発力を高く評価しており、連携を強化する。 [e004:f07] 今回、ホンダの四輪事業部門で実務経験の長い井上氏にトップ交代することで、ホンダの四輪事業の立て直しについて、系列サプライヤーとして全面的に支える体制を整える。 [e004:f08] 竹内社長もホンダ出身で、2023年7月にアステモの社長に就いた。 [e004:f09] ホンダでは財務・管理部門が長く、アステモでは前任社長時代の品質問題を踏まえた対応や財務体質の改善、株式公開に向けた準備などを担ってきた。 [e004:f10] 井上勝史氏（いのうえ・かつし）1986年3月、横浜国立大学経営学部卒、同年4月ホンダ入社。 [e004:f11] 2015年ホンダカーズインディア社長、16年ホンダ執行役員、欧州地域本部長、20年常務執行役員兼中国本部長兼本田技研工業（中国）投資総経理兼本田技研科技（中国）総経理、23年執行役専務兼電動事業開発本部長、25年取締役執行役専務兼四輪事業本部長兼リスクマネジメントオフィサー、25年6月同取締役執行役専務、26年4月同取締役。

evidence.title: Honda ZR-V Launched at Rs 47.99 Lakh
evidence.body: [e005:f01] Honda Cars India has finally launched the all-new Honda ZR-V Hybrid in the country. [e005:f02] Adding to it, deliveries of the hybrid SUV has also been commenced across India. [e005:f03] Honda ZR-V Hybrid Specs and Mileage The new ZR-V is powered by e:HEV Sports Hybrid system that combines a 2.0-litre direct injection Atkinson-cycle engine and the advanced dual-motor hybrid system with e-CVT. [e005:f04] The combined power and torque output stands at 184 hp at 5000 - 6000 rpm and 315 Nm at 2000 rpm, respectively. [e005:f05] The Honda ZR-V hybrid is claimed to offer an impressive fuel economy of 22.80 kmpl. [e005:f06] The intelligent hybrid system seamlessly switches between Electric, Hybrid and Engine Drive modes, ensuring optimal efficiency and performance across city roads, highways and varied driving conditions. [e005:f07] Colors The All-New Honda ZR-V is available in 4 colors - Twilight Mist Black Pearl, Meteoroid Gray Metallic, Platinum White Pearl and Crystal Black Pearl. [e005:f08] Warranty Details Honda is offering the all-new ZR-V with a 3-year unlimited kilometre standard warranty, 3 years complimentary RSA, extended warranty options up to 7 years, and Anytime Warranty coverage up to 10 years/ 120,000 kms. [e005:f09] The lithium-ion battery comes with an 8 year/ 160,000 km warranty (whichever is earlier), and hybrid system components are covered for 5 years/ 100,000 km (whichever is earlier). [e005:f10] Honda ZR-V Key Details The new ZR-V comes with full-LED lighting setup and rides on 18-inch alloy wheels. [e005:f11] It comes with an all-black interior scheme, leatherette upholstery, and a dual-zone climate control. [e005:f12] The SUV gets a 9-inch touchscreen infotainment unit with wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, a 10.2-inch digital driver's display, 12-speaker Bose premium audio system and wireless smartphone charging. [e005:f13] The ZR-V offers 60:40 split-fold rear seats and up to 1,313-litres of boot space with the second row folded flat. [e005:f14] It features an 8-way powered driver seat with one-touch memory function linked to the smart key fob, and a 4-way power adjustable front passenger seat. [e005:f15] The new Honda ZR-V is equipped with ADAS suite with features like Collision Mitigation Braking System, Adaptive Cruise Control, Lane Keeping Assist System and Road Departure Mitigation System. [e005:f16] For safety and security, the SUV gets an 8 airbags, 360-degree camera, vehicle stability assist, hill descent control, front and rear parking sensors and others.

evidence.title: Adrian Newey addresses Stroll red flag as Honda launches investigation
evidence.body: [e001:f01] Adrian Newey addresses Stroll setback amid Honda investigation Jamie Woodhouse 24 Jul 2026 7:11 PM Adrian Newey observing in the Aston Martin garage Adrian Newey suggested that Lance Stroll ’s suspected rear suspension failure in Hungary was not related to the Aston Martin AMR26 upgrade package. [e001:f02] Newey therefore described it as a “very unexpected” failure as Aston Martin begins its opening phase of developing the AMR26. [e001:f03] Newey also confirmed that Honda is investigating the cause of vibrations, which were reported by Fernando Alonso, and could be seen on the data. [e001:f04] In terms of pace, there were encouraging signs for Aston Martin. [e001:f05] It was a more frustrating Friday on Lance Stroll’s side of the garage. [e001:f06] Stroll triggered the red flags when he spun out of FP1. [e001:f07] Stroll did not appear in FP2, as extensive work continued on his car. [e001:f08] Adrian Newey, Aston Martin team principal and design chief, addressed the situation in Friday’s team leaders’ press conference. [e001:f09] The area of failure in question was not a part of Aston Martin’s 16-piece upgrade, Newey confirmed. [e001:f10] “Everybody is feverishly trying to understand exactly what went wrong and what happened as we speak, and it’s only once we have an understanding that we can comment on what we do next,” Newey told and others. [e001:f11] Newey explained both situations, confirming that Honda has launched an investigation into Alonso’s report. [e001:f12] “So the first question, staying away from the kerbs, that’s purely because we are acquiring aero data,” said Newey. [e001:f13] “When you’re trying to acquire aero data, you don’t want the disruption of kerbs thrown in, the inconsistency that corrupts the data.
